name: Pithla
subtitle: loose gram flour curry slackened with sour buttermilk, garlicky and made in ten minutes

ingredients.note: the sourness is the point; leave fresh buttermilk out overnight
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Whisk the besan into the cold buttermilk before anything goes on the heat. Lumps formed in a hot pan never come out.
Sour buttermilk gives pithla its character — leave fresh buttermilk on the counter overnight, or stir a squeeze of lemon into it.
Have the bhakri dough ready if you are eating it the proper way; pithla waits for nobody.

steps.text: Whisk the besan into the cold buttermilk with the turmeric and salt until completely smooth, then whisk in the water.
steps.tip: Push the slurry through a sieve if you see any lumps. Thirty seconds now saves the dish.

steps.text: Heat the oil, pop the mustard seeds, then add the cumin, curry leaves and hing.
Add the garlic and green chilli and fry 1 minute until the garlic smells sweet but has not coloured.
Add the onion, if using, and cook 4 minutes until soft.
Pour in the besan slurry in a slow stream, stirring continuously.
Bring to a gentle boil and simmer 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until it thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon and the raw besan smell is gone.
steps.tip: It thickens a lot as it cools, so pull it off looser than you want to serve it.

steps.text: Check the salt, fold through the coriander and pour into bowls.
Serve immediately with hot jowar bhakri, raw onion and a green chilli.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated but sets firm. Reheat over low heat with 3 to 4 tbsp water, whisking, until it loosens back to a pouring consistency.
